marketSummary: Indian benchmark indices posted an aggressive rebound on October 29 as the Nifty 50 surged 1.05% to reclaim 22,936.75 and the Sensex rallied 905 points to 74,151.04. The upswing was catalyzed by the US Federal Reserve's rate pause (holding benchmark rates steady at 3.75%-4.00%), modest cooling in crude prices to $114/bbl, and net institutional buying by both FIIs and DIIs. Capital goods, defence, FMCG, and private banks led the charge, offsetting overhangs from elevated crude benchmarks and rupee softness at 95.21/USD.
dailyFocus: Track post-earnings continuation setups in Trent and L&T, alongside multi-week base breakouts in defence counters (HAL, BEL, COCHINSHIP) fueled by the Defence Acquisition Council's landmark ₹2.12 lakh crore procurement clearance.

news.headline: Trent Q2 Net Profit Jumps 25.4% to ₹468 Cr; Noel Tata Retires, Bahram Vakil Appointed Chairman
news.summary: Trent Ltd reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹5,873.14 cr (+21.9% YoY) and net profit of ₹468.09 cr (+25.4% YoY) with operating EBITDA of ₹785 cr (+37% YoY). The company opened 10 Westside and 19 Zudio stores, crossing the 1,000-store milestone for Zudio. Concurrently, Noel N. Tata announced his retirement effective November 11, 2026, with Bahram Vakil appointed chairman effective November 12, 2026.
news.impact: Strong earnings beat provides structural support to absorb short-term leadership succession reactions and defend multi-week base support.

news.headline: Nifty Reclaims 22,900 as US Fed Holds Rates at 3.75%-4.00% and FIIs Turn Net Buyers
news.summary: The Nifty 50 surged 237.91 points (1.05%) to settle at 22,936.75 on October 29 after the US Federal Reserve maintained a pause on policy interest rates. Indian equity markets witnessed positive breadth with 1,484 advances to 1,284 declines, aided by dual institutional net buying from FIIs (₹871.83 cr) and DIIs (₹643.35 cr).
news.impact: Decisive index close over 22,900 validates a multi-session swing reversal, increasing the odds for technical breakouts across frontline large-caps.

news.headline: L&T Posts 33% Net Profit Surge to ₹5,202 Cr on Record Inflows of ₹1.48 Lakh Cr; Backlog Hits ₹8.53 Lakh Cr
news.summary: Larsen & Toubro reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 16% YoY to ₹78,750 cr and net profit rise of 33% YoY to ₹5,202 cr. Order intake clocked an all-time quarterly high of ₹1,47,665 cr (+28% YoY), propelling the order book to a record ₹8.53 lakh cr, with net working capital improving 850 bps YoY to 1.7% of revenue.
news.impact: Record backlog and high-volume breakout candidate capable of leading industrial momentum across Nifty heavyweights.

news.headline: CG Power Order Backlog Reaches Record ₹23,646 Cr (+58% YoY); Subsidiary Wins ₹433 Cr Kavach Deal
news.summary: CG Power reported an order backlog surge of 58% YoY to ₹23,646 cr, powered by a 78% YoY surge in quarterly inflows to ₹8,485 cr. Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to ₹3,802 cr while PAT climbed 44% YoY to ₹409 cr. Subsidiary GG Tronics simultaneously bagged a ₹433 cr on-board Kavach equipment order from Chittaranjan Locomotive Works.
news.impact: Unprecedented backlog growth and Railway Kavach integration offer fundamental justification for a cup-and-handle pattern breakout.

news.headline: Cochin Shipyard in Focus on Next-Gen Naval Warship Clearances Ahead of November Q2 Earnings
news.summary: Cochin Shipyard gained renewed traction after the DAC cleared Acceptance of Necessity for indigenous next-generation destroyers and active naval decoy systems on October 26. The yard's confirmed order book stands above ₹20,700 cr, while investors await the company's scheduled early-November board meeting for Q2 results and interim dividend consideration.
news.impact: Constructive base building above 1,120 support level with pipeline visibility acting as a catalyst into the November earnings window.

news.headline: Armed Forces Advance 200 Light Utility Helicopter Order Following ₹2.12 Lakh Cr MoD DAC Clearance
news.summary: Following the Defence Acquisition Council's (DAC) approval of capital procurements worth ₹2.12 lakh cr on October 26, the Indian Army and IAF are advancing orders for approximately 200 indigenous Light Utility Helicopters (LUH) from HAL to replace the legacy Cheetah/Chetak fleet, supplementing engine capacity expansions previously commissioned at Koraput.
news.impact: High-conviction macro procurement trigger accelerates accumulation patterns near consolidation base resistance.

news.headline: BEL Schedules Q2 Results for October 30 Amid Multi-Billion DAC Radar and EW Opportunities
news.summary: Bharat Electronics is set to consider and approve Q2 FY27 financial results on October 30, 2026. This comes on the back of securing ₹1,011 cr in fresh orders since mid-October, including a ₹770 cr MoD contract for Improved Low Level Light Weight Radars, with the company primed as the primary electronics supplier for the ₹2.12 lakh cr DAC programs.
news.impact: Scheduled Q2 results act as an immediate volatility catalyst with technical setups pressing against key overhead supply bands.

news.headline: Asian Paints Q2 Net Profit Grows 7.5% to ₹1,068 Cr; Announces ₹5.75 Interim Dividend
news.summary: Asian Paints reported its Q2 FY27 results on October 29, clocking consolidated net profit of ₹1,068 cr (+7.5% YoY) on revenue of ₹9,954 cr (+17% YoY). The board announced an interim dividend of ₹5.75 per share, though operating margins faced moderate drag from input cost and crude derivatives inflation.
news.impact: Revenue growth meets expectations but margin containment leaves the stock rangebound within its existing medium-term trading channel.

news.headline: Adani Ports Leads Nifty 50 Rallies on Heavy Cargo Volumes and Broad Infrastructure Participation
news.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone emerged among the top percentage gainers in the Nifty 50 on October 29 as infrastructure stocks witnessed aggressive short-covering following L&T's upbeat project execution commentary and strong quarterly volume momentum across Indian marine hubs.
news.impact: High-volume surge off ascending trendline support favors short-term continuation toward prior swing highs.

news.headline: Brent Crude Retraces Towards $114/bbl Bringing Selective Respite to Downstream Consuming Sectors
news.summary: Brent crude futures declined 1% to trade near $114 per barrel on October 29 as immediate Middle East geopolitical escalation fears moderated slightly. Despite the day's easing, crude remains elevated on a monthly horizon, continuing to exert pressure on the Indian rupee (₹95.21/USD) and testing margins for downstream logistics, aviation, and paints.
news.impact: Cooling energy prices relieve margin anxiety in paints and retail logistics, but high absolute crude levels keep upside targets measured.
